evidence: Women's Worlds (6 theses) and The History of British Women's Writing, 1690-1750 (1) are Ros Ballaster's works; Ros is Rosalind Margaret Ballaster. The 1991 'et al' entry is probably a fragment of Women's Worlds; the zero-weight novel chapter is also hers.

All four entries are versions or fragments of Armed and Dangerous: From Undercover Struggle to Freedom, the autobiography of Ronald (Ronnie) Kasrils. The apparent additional author in the last entry is a parsing artifact.
The sole title, Rome's Economic Revolution (2014; 8 theses), is explicitly credited to Philip Kay by Oxford University Press; Ph abbreviates Philip.

other_people: Joaquim António de Carvalho e Menezes
evidence: Igrejas e irmandades de Ouro Preto (6) is by Joaquim Furtado de Menezes and is issue 1 of Publicações do IEPHA, explaining the 1975 series-title fragment (1). Demonstração geográfica e política do território (1) is by Joaquim António de Carvalho e Menezes: approximately 7/8 belong to the LC person.

Dicionário de Regionalismos do Rio Grande do Sul (6) is by Zeno Cardoso Nunes and Rui Cardoso Nunes. Euro = Neoliberalismo + Socialismo (1) is by Rui José da Conceição Nunes; História da educação no Renascimento (1) is by Ruy Afonso da Costa Nunes. LC share: 6/8.
The sole title, Formação de uma economia periférica: o caso do Paraná (1981; 8 theses), is Pedro Calil Padis's book. Calili in the LC heading is a spelling variant, not evidence of another author.

Anne Orthwood's Bastard (5) is by John Ruston Pagan. The two Glasgow midwifery papers (1 each) are John Macmichan Pagan's; Annals of Ayr (1) is John H. Pagan's; Glasgow Past and Present (1) was edited by James Pagan. The LC share is 5/9 listed work-thesis counts, below the brief's mostly threshold but not a minority; verdict held unclear for this intermediate split.

Athenian Myths and Festivals (5), Altars with Palm-Trees, Palm-Trees and Parthenoi (2), and Herodotos (and others) on Pelasgians (1) are all explicitly credited to Christiane Sourvinou-Inwood by their publishers. Chr abbreviates Christiane.

The Church in an Age of Revolution, The Modernist Movement in the Roman Church, and Secular Despair and Christian Faith are Alec R. (Alexander Roper) Vidler's books. The 1939 Editorial also fits his documented editorship of Theology beginning that year.
The Education of the New-Canadian (1918; all 7 theses) is by James Thomas Milton Anderson, as the University of Regina library confirms. Janies is a transcription error for James.
